title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Premium Revision Paper #4

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #4
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is a stem that stores food and is eaten or used for sugar? (1 mark)
   A. Tomato
   B. Bean pod
   C. Sugarcane
   D. Sukuma wiki leaf

2. Which is the best way of studying how a seedling grows? (1 mark)
   A. Measure its height every two days
   B. Never water it
   C. Cover it in sand
   D. Pull it up daily

3. Which of these plant parts is usually colourful? (1 mark)
   A. Root
   B. Flower
   C. Soil
   D. Stem

4. Which of these is a difference between plants and animals? (1 mark)
   A. Plants die but animals do not
   B. Plants breathe and animals do not
   C. Animals move from place to place and take in ready-made food
   D. Animals do not grow

5. A bat flies but has fur and feeds its babies milk. What is it? (1 mark)
   A. A mammal
   B. A bird
   C. A reptile
   D. An insect

6. Which part takes back most of the water from the leftover food? (1 mark)
   A. Stomach
   B. Gullet
   C. Mouth
   D. Large intestine

7. Why should you limit sweets and sugary drinks? (1 mark)
   A. They make you taller
   B. They cause tooth decay
   C. They help digestion
   D. They make teeth stronger

8. Which of these parts is found after the stomach? (1 mark)
   A. Gullet
   B. Small intestine
   C. Mouth
   D. Tongue

9. What does the small intestine mainly absorb? (1 mark)
   A. Digested food
   B. Light
   C. Air
   D. Sound

10. Why should you wear shoes and wash hands to prevent worms? (1 mark)
   A. Water makes worms grow
   B. Worm eggs are found in dirty soil and on dirty hands
   C. Shoes make food digest
   D. Worms live in shoes

11. What does the gullet do? (1 mark)
   A. Stores faeces
   B. Makes saliva
   C. Absorbs food into blood
   D. Pushes swallowed food to the stomach

12. Which of these is a healthy habit for digestion? (1 mark)
   A. Eating food that fell in dirt
   B. Never washing fruits
   C. Drinking water from a dirty pond
   D. Washing hands before eating

13. What is the job of the anus? (1 mark)
   A. To let faeces leave the body
   B. To make saliva
   C. To digest food
   D. To swallow food

14. Which of these statements about matter is correct? (1 mark)
   A. Only liquids have mass
   B. Only solids have mass
   C. Solids, liquids and gases all have mass
   D. Gases have no mass

15. How many millilitres are in 2 litres? (1 mark)
   A. 2000
   B. 200
   C. 20
   D. 20 000

16. Why should each child use their own balloon for the balloon activity? (1 mark)
   A. To make it heavier
   B. To avoid spreading germs
   C. To make the balloon bigger
   D. To make it burst

17. Which activity shows that air takes up space? (1 mark)
   A. Blowing up a balloon
   B. Shining a torch
   C. Singing a song
   D. Lighting a candle

18. How many grams are in 5 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 50 000
   B. 5000
   C. 50
   D. 500

19. How many millilitres are in 1 litre? (1 mark)
   A. 10
   B. 10 000
   C. 1000
   D. 100

20. What does reuse mean? (1 mark)
   A. Bury it
   B. Throw it away
   C. Burn it
   D. Use something again

21. A wrapper of biscuits is made of plastic. Which type of waste is it? (1 mark)
   A. Non-decomposable
   B. Gas
   C. Liquid
   D. Decomposable

22. What is the danger of leaving plastic bags on the ground? (1 mark)
   A. They grow into plants
   B. They make the soil rich
   C. They stay for a long time and block drains
   D. They turn into soil fast

23. What can leak from old batteries and pollute soil and water? (1 mark)
   A. Milk
   B. Sweet juice
   C. Clean water
   D. Harmful chemicals

24. Which living things help waste to decompose? (1 mark)
   A. Fungi and bacteria
   B. Bottles
   C. Stones
   D. Plastic bags

25. What does water conservation mean? (1 mark)
   A. Selling water
   B. Boiling water
   C. Wasting water
   D. Using water carefully and protecting water sources

26. Why should a rainwater tank be covered? (1 mark)
   A. To make it rain
   B. To make water heavier
   C. To keep out mosquitoes and dirt
   D. To keep the water warm

27. Who should monitor taps in a school? (1 mark)
   A. Only visitors
   B. Water monitors
   C. Only cooks
   D. Nobody

28. What is the job of the gutter in rainwater harvesting? (1 mark)
   A. Carries water from the roof to a pipe
   B. Heats water
   C. Stores water
   D. Cleans water

29. What effect does friction have on rubbing your hands? (1 mark)
   A. It makes them warm
   B. It makes them cold
   C. It makes them wet
   D. It makes them heavy

30. Which of these needs friction to work? (1 mark)
   A. Walking on the ground
   B. A rolling wheel
   C. Skating on wet ice
   D. Sliding on oil

31. What is weight? (1 mark)
   A. The pull of gravity on an object
   B. The colour of an object
   C. The amount of light
   D. The heat of an object

32. Which of these is a problem caused by friction? (1 mark)
   A. Lighting a match
   B. Walking safely
   C. Braking a bicycle
   D. Wearing away of shoes and tyres

33. Which force makes it hard to push a heavy box along a rough floor? (1 mark)
   A. Colour
   B. Light
   C. Sound
   D. Friction

34. A stone and a crumpled paper are dropped together. They land almost together because (1 mark)
   A. There is no gravity
   B. The paper is heavier
   C. The stone is lighter
   D. Gravity pulls both and air pushes little on the crumpled paper

35. Which of these gives artificial light by burning paraffin? (1 mark)
   A. Lightning
   B. Sun
   C. Paraffin lamp
   D. Star

36. Which of these is a safety use of light? (1 mark)
   A. Colouring paint
   B. Making shadows
   C. Making sound
   D. Street lights

37. Why should candles and paraffin lamps be kept away from curtains? (1 mark)
   A. They make curtains bright
   B. They make curtains dry
   C. They can start a fire
   D. They make curtains cold

38. Which of these artificial sources charges its battery in the sun? (1 mark)
   A. Sun
   B. Solar lamp
   C. Stars
   D. Lightning

39. A lighthouse is used to (1 mark)
   A. Dry clothes
   B. Cook food
   C. Warn ships of danger
   D. Grow plants

40. Heat always moves from (1 mark)
   A. A wet place to a dry place
   B. A cooler place to a hotter place
   C. A dark place to a bright place
   D. A hotter place to a cooler place

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Describe how rainwater can be harvested from a school roof. (3 marks)

42. Explain why we should reduce friction in machines and how it can be done. (5 marks)

43. Explain why we should wash our hands before eating and after using the toilet. (3 marks)

44. A pupil says that empty containers have nothing inside. Explain why the pupil is wrong and how you would show it. (5 marks)

45. Describe what you would put in a portfolio about vertebrates and invertebrates. (4 marks)

46. List four signs of life in plants. (2 marks)

47. Give three problems caused by friction. (3 marks)

48. Give two symptoms of an unhealthy digestive system. (2 marks)

49. List four water-saving habits that pupils can practise at school. (4 marks)

50. Explain the dangers of solid waste to health, animals and the environment. (5 marks)

51. Describe the differences between mammals and birds. (4 marks)

52. Give two reasons why solids are useful in daily life. (2 marks)

53. Explain why a spider is not an insect. (3 marks)

54. State two uses of heat at home. (2 marks)

55. Group these into solid, liquid and gas: milk, chalk, oxygen, cooking oil, book, steam. (4 marks)

56. Why is the moon not a source of light? (2 marks)

57. Give two examples of decomposable waste and two of non-decomposable waste. (2 marks)

58. Explain why heat from the sun is important to the Earth. (3 marks)

59. State any four signs of life in animals. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #4 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Sugarcane
   Sugarcane stems store sugar.

2. A — Measure its height every two days
   Measuring height regularly shows growth over time.

3. B — Flower
   Flowers are often brightly coloured.

4. C — Animals move from place to place and take in ready-made food
   Most animals move about and eat food, while plants make their own food.

5. A — A mammal
   The fur and milk feeding make it a mammal.

6. D — Large intestine
   The large intestine takes back water.

7. B — They cause tooth decay
   Sugar feeds germs that damage teeth.

8. B — Small intestine
   Food moves from the stomach to the small intestine.

9. A — Digested food
   Digested food passes through its wall into blood.

10. B — Worm eggs are found in dirty soil and on dirty hands
   Worm eggs can enter the body through dirt.

11. D — Pushes swallowed food to the stomach
   The gullet squeezes food down.

12. D — Washing hands before eating
   Clean hands prevent germs from entering the mouth.

13. A — To let faeces leave the body
   The anus is the opening at the end of the digestive tube.

14. C — Solids, liquids and gases all have mass
   All matter has mass, whatever its state.

15. A — 2000
   2 x 1000 = 2000 ml.

16. B — To avoid spreading germs
   Sharing a balloon that has been in someone's mouth can spread germs.

17. A — Blowing up a balloon
   The balloon swells because air takes up space inside.

18. B — 5000
   5 x 1000 = 5000 g.

19. C — 1000
   1 litre is 1000 ml.

20. D — Use something again
   To reuse is to use again.

21. A — Non-decomposable
   Plastic wrappers do not rot easily.

22. C — They stay for a long time and block drains
   Plastic bags stay for years and block drains.

23. D — Harmful chemicals
   Old batteries have harmful chemicals.

24. A — Fungi and bacteria
   Decomposers such as fungi and bacteria break down waste.

25. D — Using water carefully and protecting water sources
   Conservation means saving water and using it wisely.

26. C — To keep out mosquitoes and dirt
   A cover stops mosquitoes breeding and dirt getting in.

27. B — Water monitors
   Monitors help make sure taps are closed.

28. A — Carries water from the roof to a pipe
   Gutters catch water as it runs off the roof.

29. A — It makes them warm
   Friction produces heat.

30. A — Walking on the ground
   Walking needs grip from friction.

31. A — The pull of gravity on an object
   Weight is the pull of gravity on a thing.

32. D — Wearing away of shoes and tyres
   Friction wears surfaces away.

33. D — Friction
   Rough floor gives large friction.

34. D — Gravity pulls both and air pushes little on the crumpled paper
   The air has very little effect on the crumpled paper.

35. C — Paraffin lamp
   A paraffin lamp is a made light source.

36. D — Street lights
   Street lights help people see at night.

37. C — They can start a fire
   Flames can set cloth on fire.

38. B — Solar lamp
   A solar lamp is made by people.

39. C — Warn ships of danger
   Lighthouses show ships where land or rocks are.

40. D — A hotter place to a cooler place
   Heat moves from hot to cold.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Rain falls on the roof and runs into the gutter. The gutter leads to a pipe which fills a covered tank.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for roof and gutter, 1 mark for pipe, 1 mark for tank.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: Friction wears out parts, wastes energy and makes machines hot. It is reduced by oiling, smoothing, using rollers or ball bearings.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for reasons and 3 marks for methods.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Hands may carry germs and worm eggs. Washing removes them and stops them entering the mouth and causing disease.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for germs on hands, 1 mark for washing removes them, 1 mark for preventing illness.

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: They are full of air which is matter. Air takes up space. For example the upside-down cup pushed into water stays dry inside or a balloon swells with air.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for air inside, 1 mark for air is matter, 1 mark for an activity, 1 mark for the observation, 1 mark for the conclusion.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: A drawing of each animal, its name, whether it is a vertebrate or invertebrate, one sign of life seen, put together in a folder.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four items.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: Any four of: grow, reproduce, remove waste, respond to changes, die.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two correct signs and 2 marks for four correct signs.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: It wears away shoes and tyres, wastes energy, makes machines hot and slows moving parts.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: Stomach ache, bloating, diarrhoea, vomiting, constipation, worms (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: Close taps, report leaks, use a bucket for watering the garden, water plants in the morning or evening, use a cup to drink.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

50. (5 marks)
   Answer: Health: flies and rats spread diseases, mosquitoes breed in tins. Animals: goats eat polythene and die. Environment: blocked drains, polluted water, harmful smoke from burning.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for health, 1 mark for animals and 2 marks for environment.

51. (4 marks)
   Answer: Mammals have hair or fur and feed their young on milk and most give birth to live young. Birds have feathers and wings and lay eggs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four differences.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: They keep their shape so we can build houses, make tools, furniture, clothes and shoes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct use.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: Insects have six legs and three body parts. A spider has eight legs, so it is not an insect. It is an invertebrate.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for six legs, 1 mark for eight legs, 1 mark for conclusion.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: Cooking, warming, ironing, drying clothes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: Solids: chalk and book. Liquids: milk and cooking oil. Gases: oxygen and steam.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: It does not make its own light. It reflects light from the sun.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for no light of its own and 1 mark for reflecting sunlight.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: Decomposable: vegetable peelings, dung, leaves. Non-decomposable: plastic, tin, glass.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: It warms the Earth so plants and animals can live, it dries things, and helps the water cycle.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of three points.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: Feeding, growing, breathing, reproducing, removing waste, moving, responding to changes, dying (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two correct signs and 2 marks for four.
